verses.text: Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother was Abijah, daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his ancestor David had done.
In the first month of the first year of his rule, he opened the doors of the LORD's temple and repaired them.
He brought in the priests and Levites and gathered them in the open square on the east side.
He said to them, "Listen to me, Levites! Make yourselves holy now, and make holy the temple of the LORD, the God of your ancestors. Take all the filth out of the holy place.
Our ancestors were unfaithful. They did evil in the eyes of the LORD our God and left him. They turned their faces away from the place where the LORD lives and turned their backs on him.
They shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps. They did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
So the LORD has been angry with Judah and Jerusalem. He has made them something that frightens people, something they are shocked at and make fun of, as you can see with your own eyes.
That is why our fathers were killed in battle, and our sons, daughters, and wives have been taken as prisoners.
Now I have decided to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that his fierce anger will turn away from us.
My sons, do not be careless now. The LORD has chosen you to stand in front of him and serve him, to be his servants and to burn incense to him."

Then these Levites got ready to work. From the family of Kohath: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah. From the family of Merari: Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel. From the family of Gershon: Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah.
From the family of Elizaphan: Shimri and Jeuel. From the family of Asaph: Zechariah and Mattaniah.
From the family of Heman: Jehuel and Shimei. From the family of Jeduthun: Shemaiah and Uzziel.
They gathered their relatives, made themselves holy, and went in to clean the LORD's temple, as the king had ordered, following the LORD's words.

The priests went into the inner part of the LORD's temple to clean it. They brought out into the temple courtyard everything unclean they found in the LORD's temple. The Levites took it and carried it out to the Kidron Valley.

They began the work of making the temple holy on the first day of the first month. On the eighth day of the month they reached the LORD's porch. They spent eight more days making the LORD's temple holy, and they finished on the sixteenth day of the first month.

Then they went to King Hezekiah in the palace and said, "We have cleaned the whole temple of the LORD, the altar for burnt offerings with all its tools, and the table for the holy bread with all its things.
We have also prepared and made holy all the things King Ahaz threw away while he was king and unfaithful to God. Look, they are in front of the LORD's altar."
Early the next morning King Hezekiah gathered the city leaders and went up to the LORD's temple.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the temple, and for Judah. The king told the priests, the descendants of Aaron, to offer them on the LORD's altar.

So the priests killed the bulls, collected the blood, and sprinkled it on the altar. They killed the rams and sprinkled their blood on the altar. They killed the lambs and sprinkled their blood on the altar.
Then they brought the male goats for the sin offering to the king and the people, and they laid their hands on them.

The priests killed the goats and put their blood on the altar as a sin offering, to make all Israel right with God. The king had ordered that the burnt offering and the sin offering be made for all Israel.

Hezekiah placed the Levites in the LORD's temple with cymbals, harps, and lyres, as David, Gad the king's seer, and the prophet Nathan had commanded. This command came from the LORD through his prophets.
The Levites stood ready with David's instruments, and the priests with their trumpets.
Hezekiah ordered them to offer the burnt offering on the altar. As the burnt offering began, the song to the LORD also began, with trumpets and the instruments of David king of Israel.
All the people worshiped, the singers sang, and the trumpets played until the burnt offering was finished.
When the offerings were finished, the king and everyone with him bowed down and worshiped.
King Hezekiah and the leaders told the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. So they sang praises with joy, and they bowed down and worshiped.

Then Hezekiah said, "Now you have given yourselves to the LORD. Come and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the LORD's temple." So the people brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and everyone who wanted to brought burnt offerings.
The people brought seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs. All these were burnt offerings to the LORD.
The other animals set apart as holy offerings were six hundred cattle and three thousand sheep.

But there were not enough priests to skin all the burnt offerings. So their relatives the Levites helped them until the work was done and until more priests had made themselves holy. The Levites had been more careful to make themselves holy than the priests.
There were many burnt offerings, along with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings that went with each burnt offering. So the service of the LORD's temple was set up again.
Hezekiah and all the people were full of joy at what God had done for the people, because it had all happened so quickly.
